title: Double-clicking a grade button drops the next card without ever grading it
detail: grade() closes over `queue` and reads queue[0]. Two clicks landing before the re-render both resolve `current` to the same card, upsert it twice, and each call setQueue(rest => rest.slice(1)) — so two cards leave the session while only the first is scheduled. The second is silently skipped and will not reappear until it happens to come due again. The grade buttons have no disabled state during the await.

title: A repo failure pins the page on its loading spinner forever
detail: reload() has no try/catch, so a rejection from listDue skips setIsLoading(false) entirely. The identical pattern exists in useLibrary.reload (line 32) — any IndexedDB error leaves the library permanently in its loading state with no message and no retry.

title: A card with an empty options array deadlocks the review session permanently
detail: No option buttons render, so `selected` stays null, `isAnswered` stays false, and the grade buttons never appear. The card sits at the head of the queue with no skip, no dismiss and no way past it — every future review session opens on the same dead card.

title: Options are keyed by their own text
detail: key={option} collides whenever the model emits two identical options, which produces React key warnings and can attach the wrong selection state to a button.

title: Finishing a session shows the same 'Nothing due' empty state as never having started one
detail: There is no completion summary — no count of what was reviewed, no accuracy, no sense of having finished. The reward for clearing a deck is identical to the screen you would see if the deck were empty.

title: Grade button hover states are light-only
detail: Each GRADES entry pairs bg/text with dark variants but leaves hover:bg-*-100 unpaired, so hovering in dark mode washes the button back to a light colour.

title: No keyboard grading in a keyboard-shaped task
detail: Spaced repetition is a rapid-fire keyboard activity everywhere it exists; here all four grades require a mouse click, and the options themselves have no number shortcuts.
